tei:titleStmt.tei:title: Prayer of the Guest Chaplain of the U.S. House of Representatives: Rabbi Claudio Kogan on 10 June 2015

tei:div.tei:head: Prayer of the Guest Chaplain of the U.S. House of Representatives: Rabbi Claudio Kogan on 10 June 2015

tei:lg.tei:l: Our God and God of our ancestors,
God of compassion,
God of justice,
and God of peace.
In this great Hall where dreams come true,
we ask Your blessings upon these great men and women,
the Representatives of the people.
They have devoted their lives to our welfare.
Give them wisdom and courage.
Inspire them with the teachings of our prophets,
as they answer Isaiah’s call
to feed the hungry and clothe the naked,
Jeremiah’s request
to protect the orphan and the widow,
and Ezekiel’s plea
to lift up those who cannot stand on their own
in this land
and all lands.
As an immigrant who came to this country 16 years ago
and became an American citizen just 2 years ago,
I join this House in a prayer
of profound gratitude and deep appreciation
for the blessings we,
the people of the United States of America,
are privileged to enjoy.
I ask You, God,
to let the lights of truth and harmony
shine from this Chamber
as beacons for the betterment of all Americans.
Amen.

tei:note.tei:p: Reference unknown. Cf. Psalms 145:14 and Exodus 23:5. Perhaps the end of Ezekiel 21:31? If you know the reference, please let us know in the comments.
